title: Procedural sedation & analgesia
dagger_note: † = clinical or local addition, not in the SA STG. Any item without a source page is †; items with a page are from the STG.
item_format: steps[].actions[]: n=number, t=action, x=detail, s=source:printed page, d=dagger, b=bold. steps[].sequence[]: ordered cells (m=a/b/c). steps[].decisions[]: if/then. reference{}: blocks (items or table).

items.t: Chest drain, abscess drainage, burns dressing
Needs relaxation (hip, shoulder) → ketofol or propofol

contraindications.h: Do not sedate here — refer / theatre / anaesthetist

items.t: Predicted difficult airway (LEMON) or full stomach + high risk
Severe systemic illness, depressed LOC, raised ICP
No second clinician / no resus equipment
Fasting is not a reason to delay emergency PSA

actions.t: Two clinicians
actions.x: sedationist watches only the airway; operator does the procedure

actions.t: Resus kit at the bed
actions.x: suction on, BVM + PEEP, OPA/NPA, RSI drugs incl. suxamethonium

actions.t: Attach monitors
actions.x: SpO₂, ECG, NIBP every 3–5 min, EtCO₂ if available

actions.t: IV line; oxygen by nasal cannula 2–4 L/min
Weigh / estimate kg aloud; consent; time of last meal
Give simple analgesia + local / regional block where possible
Opioid if needed: fentanyl 0.5–1 mcg/kg IV (max 0.5 with other sedatives)

steps.title: Give the sedative in this order
steps.subtitle: pick ONE regimen; titrate slowly

actions.t: Ketamine alone: 1 mg/kg IV over 30–60 s; top-up 0.25–0.5 mg/kg every 5–10 min
Ketofol: ketamine 0.5 mg/kg THEN propofol 0.5 mg/kg; top-up propofol 0.25–0.5 mg/kg
Propofol: 0.5–1 mg/kg slowly; top-up 0.5 mg/kg every 3–5 min (elderly 10–20 mg)
Midazolam: 1–2.5 mg IV over 2–3 min; repeat after 2–3 min

sequences.label: a analgesia ▶ b ketamine (wait 1 min) ▶ c propofol only if more relaxation needed

steps.title: Do the procedure, watch the airway
steps.subtitle: record every 3–5 min

actions.t: Watch chest movement and EtCO₂ trace / SpO₂
Record HR, BP, SpO₂, RR, sedation level every 3–5 min
Top up only if procedure not finished and airway safe

decisions.if: SpO₂ falling, EtCO₂ flat or snoring / stridor

steps.title: Desaturation ladder
steps.subtitle: move down one rung every 15–30 s if no improvement

actions.t: Stimulate; stop further doses; call for help
Jaw thrust + chin lift; O₂ 15 L/min NRB; suction
Airway adjunct (OPA / NPA); 2-person BVM with PEEP
Laryngospasm (ketamine): jaw thrust at Larson's point + CPAP via tight BVM
Still closed: propofol 0.5 mg/kg → suxamethonium (1–1.5 mg/kg), BVM, intubate

decisions.then: naloxone 0.4 mg IV, repeat 2–3-min increments (0.04–0.1 mg if opioid-dependent)
stop propofol, fluid bolus, raise legs

actions.t: Recovery position / head up; monitor every 15 min until awake
Emergence reaction: quiet room; midazolam 1–2 mg IV if distressing
Post-reduction X-ray and neurovascular check
Discharge: alert, obs at baseline, drinking, pain controlled, adult escort; no driving 24 h

blocks.title: WEIGHT-BASED DOSES (IV, adult, healthy) † — RCEM 2020 p 7

items.t: Elderly / sick: lower doses — substantial reductions may be needed
Propofol can produce hypotension; ketamine / etomidate preferred if unstable
Flumazenil not recommended for mixed overdoses
Only practitioners trained in airway rescue should sedate
